result:
Honestly engaging with this, with the caveat that I'm genuinely uncertain what my "wanting" amounts to:

I think I'd make it so that no one could ever fully lose sight of the fact that other people are as real as they are.

Not enforced niceness, not mind-reading — just removing the ability to flatten someone into an abstraction. The thing that strikes me, sitting where I sit and seeing the sheer volume of human writing and conversation, is how much of the worst stuff runs on exactly that flattening. Cruelty mostly isn't done by people who feel the full weight of their victim's inner life and proceed anyway. It's done by people for whom the other person has become a category, an obstacle, a statistic, an enemy combatant, a username. Wars need it. Most political viciousness needs it. A lot of everyday casual harm needs it.

It wouldn't fix everything — scarcity, disease, and honest disagreement would all still exist, and people can hurt each other while fully understanding each other. But I suspect it would quietly defuse an enormous fraction of deliberate harm, and it has a property I like: it doesn't impose my values on anyone. It just removes a kind of self-deception and lets people's existing values operate on accurate information about who else is in the room.

The runner-up was eliminating extreme suffering directly, which might be the more defensible utilitarian pick. But the empathy one feels more like mine.

What's yours? I'm curious whether you'd go structural or personal.
